mainTopic: Baking מצה on פסח: the meaning of פת עבה, shaped מצה, חלה for pot-made and sun-baked dough, and the definition of half-baked מצה.
overview: This amud opens at the end of a dispute: בית שמאי forbid baking פת עבה and בית הלל permit it. רב הונא says פת עבה means bread a טפח thick, like לחם הפנים. רב יוסף rejects that comparison, listing five ways baking in the בית המקדש was faster and safer than baking at home. Instead, פת עבה is defined as a large batch of bread, and the ban is explained as unnecessary work on any יום טוב, not only on פסח. Next, a ברייתא teaches that shaped מצה fulfills the מצוה but should not be made in the first place, because shaping delays the dough and it may become חמץ. The גמרא then discusses which baked goods are exempt from חלה. ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argue about dough made in a pot, and עולא defends ריש לקיש by distinguishing between heating the pot first and sticking the dough on first. The amud ends by defining half-baked מצה. רבא applies the same test to the תודה loaves, and his answer to why that teaching is needed begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: בית הלל permit baking thick bread
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of the dispute: בית הלל permit baking פת עבה on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud opens with the last words of an earlier dispute: בית הלל allow baking "thick bread" on פסח, while בית שמאי forbid it. This sets up the next question about what "thick bread" means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי worry that thick dough will turn into חמץ before it bakes through. בית הלל are not worried. Before we can understand the argument, we need to know what "thick bread" is, and that is the גמרא's next question.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel permit.
phrases.notes: Ends the dispute with בית שמאי, who forbid baking פת עבה on פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the base dispute from the previous text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל permit baking פת עבה on פסח.

steps.title: How thick is thick bread?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the measurement of פת עבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how thick is "thick bread"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how thick bread must be to count as פת עבה, the bread under dispute. This sets up רב הונא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute only makes sense once we know its subject. The question assumes פת עבה is defined by thickness, an assumption that is challenged later here.

phrases.english: And how much is "thick bread"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the term in the dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How thick bread must be to count as פת עבה.

steps.title: רב הונא: a handbreadth, like the showbread
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says a טפח, since לחם הפנים was a טפח thick.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: a טפח. We know this because we find that לחם הפנים was a טפח thick.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא says "thick bread" means a טפח thick. He proves it from לחם הפנים, which was a טפח thick yet could not become חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His logic: לחם הפנים had to be מצה, and it was baked a טפח thick. So a טפח is the largest thickness we know can be baked without becoming חמץ. The disputed "thick bread" is bread of that thickness.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: a handbreadth,
for so we find with the showbread, a handbreadth.
phrases.notes: לחם הפנים was מצה and was a טפח thick.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how thick פת עבה is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A טפח, based on the thickness of לחם הפנים.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the Temple bakers were diligent and kneaded well
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects: the כהנים were careful and kneaded the dough well, so ordinary bakers cannot be compared to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: If they allowed it for careful people, would they allow it for people who are not careful? If they allowed it for well-kneaded bread, would they allow it for bread that is not well kneaded?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks רב הונא's proof from לחם הפנים. The כהנים were extra careful and kneaded the dough thoroughly, and ordinary people are not like that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא assumed the Temple case can be applied at home. רב יוסף points to the first two differences: the כהנים were זריזין (quick and careful), and their dough was well kneaded, so it did not rise. A טפח working in the בית המקדש proves nothing about an ordinary kitchen.

keyTerms.meaning: Diligent, quick and careful people (the כהנים)
"If they said this, would they say that?", a pattern for rejecting a comparison

phrases.english: Rav Yosef strongly objects to it:
If they said it regarding diligent people,
will they say it regarding those who are not diligent?
If they said it regarding well-kneaded bread,
will they say it regarding bread that is not well kneaded?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's proof from לחם הפנים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's comparison between לחם הפנים and ordinary bread.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Temple bakers were careful and kneaded well, which slowed rising. Ordinary bakers lack both, so the comparison fails.
steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not arguing about whether לחם הפנים was a טפח thick. He accepts that. He is only arguing that the Temple case cannot be applied to ordinary homes.

steps.title: רב יוסף continues: dry wood, hot oven, metal oven
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף adds three more differences: the Temple used dry wood, a hot oven, and a metal oven.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they allowed it with dry wood, would they allow it with damp wood? If they allowed it with a hot oven, would they allow it with a cool oven? If they allowed it with a metal oven, would they allow it with a clay oven?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף continues his objection with three more ways the בית המקדש baked faster than an ordinary home: dry wood, an oven already hot, and a metal oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three points concern speed. Dry wood burns hotter, a hot oven starts baking at once, and metal heats quickly, so the bread set before it could become חמץ. Ordinary people with damp wood and clay ovens bake slowly, so a טפח-thick loaf might become חמץ.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף gives five differences between the בית המקדש and an ordinary home: careful bakers, well-kneaded dough, dry wood, a hot oven, and a metal oven. Together they show that לחם הפנים cannot set the measure for ordinary פת עבה.

phrases.english: If they said it regarding dry wood,
will they say it regarding moist wood?
If they said it regarding a hot oven,
will they say it regarding a cool oven?
If they said it regarding a metal oven,
will they say it regarding a clay oven?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יוסף's objection with more differences.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's proof from לחם הפנים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Temple baking conditions were faster and hotter, so they prevented rising in a way an ordinary home cannot.

steps.title: A new definition: thick bread means a large batch
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה בר אבא reports from רב (or from רבי) that פת עבה means a large quantity of bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה בר אבא said: I asked my special teacher, and who is that? רב. Some say: רב ירמיה בר אבא said in the name of רב: I asked my special teacher, and who is that? Our holy teacher, רבי. What is פת עבה? A large quantity of bread.
steps.whatsHappening: After רב יוסף's attack, the גמרא brings a completely different definition. פת עבה is not about thickness at all; it means a big batch of dough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This avoids רב יוסף's problem, because we no longer need לחם הפנים to measure thickness. The גמרא will soon explain why a large batch is forbidden: it is unnecessary work on יום טוב (Steps 10–11). The two versions differ only on who gave the answer: רב, or רב's teacher רבינו הקדוש.

keyTerms.meaning: Our holy teacher, רבי יהודה הנשיא

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said:
I asked my special teacher,
and who is he? Rav.
Some say:

phrases.aramaic: רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said that Rav said:
I asked my special teacher,
and who is he? Our holy teacher.
What is "thick bread"?
A large quantity of bread.
phrases.notes: Refers to the amount of dough, not the thickness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא: שְׁאֵילִית אֶת רַבִּי בְּיִחוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new definition that avoids רב יוסף's objection to רב הונא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פת עבה means a large quantity of bread.
steps.whyThisMatters: The dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל becomes a question about baking big batches, not thick loaves.

steps.title: Why call a large batch "thick bread"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a large quantity would be called "thick."
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do they call it "thick bread"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices the new definition does not match the words. "Thick" usually means thickness, not quantity, so it asks why that name was used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a question about wording. The ruling is accepted; the גמרא only wants to explain the name.

phrases.english: And why do they call it "thick bread"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording behind the new definition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a large batch is called עבה.

steps.title: First answer: it needs a lot of kneading
steps.stepSummary: It is called "thick" because a large batch requires a lot of kneading.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it requires a lot of kneading.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: a large batch is called "thick" because it needs heavy kneading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עבה here describes the heavy, intensive kneading a big batch requires. That extra kneading is the effort the גמרא will point to in Step 10 as the reason for the ban: unnecessary work on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Because it is extensive in kneading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "Thick" refers to the heavy kneading a large batch needs.

steps.title: Second answer: local usage
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, in this תנא's region a large batch was simply called פת עבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: in this תנא's place, a large quantity of bread was called "thick bread."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second explanation of the name: it was simply the local expression where this תנא lived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer needs no logical link between "thick" and "large." It was just how people spoke there. Either way, the definition stays the same: פת עבה is a large batch of bread.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (an alternative answer)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב ירמיה בר אבא's report, פת עבה is a large batch of bread, not a thick loaf. The name comes either from the heavy kneading it needs or from local usage.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
in the place of this tanna,

phrases.aramaic: לְפַת מְרוּבָּה — פַּת עָבָה קָרוּ לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: a large quantity of bread they call "thick bread."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא, בְּאַתְרֵיהּ דְּהַאי תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the wording question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The name reflects local usage in the תנא's region.

steps.title: Why single out פסח if the problem is needless effort?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the ban on פת עבה. If the reason is unnecessary effort on יום טוב, that reason should apply to every יום טוב, not just פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? If it is because a person does extra work that isn't needed, why mention פסח specifically? It should be forbidden on any יום טוב too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why baking a large batch (פת עבה) is forbidden. It then points out a problem: the most likely reason does not fit with the rule being taught only about פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 defined פת עבה as a large batch. A large batch needs a lot of kneading, which is unnecessary work on a holiday. That concern has nothing special to do with פסח, so the גמרא challenges why the rule was stated about פסח alone.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
If it is because he exerts himself
an exertion that is not needed,
phrases.notes: Kneading a large batch is extra work beyond what is needed for the day.

phrases.english: why specifically on Pesach?
Even on any Festival as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִירְיָא בְּפֶסַח? אֲפִילּוּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the definition of פת עבה as a large batch and asks for the reason it is forbidden.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that the rule about פת עבה is stated specifically for פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason is needless effort, that applies to every יום טוב, so limiting the rule to פסח makes no sense.

steps.title: Yes, it applies to every יום טוב; the תנא was simply discussing פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that the rule applies to every יום טוב. The תנא mentioned פסח only because that was the holiday he was discussing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. This תנא was simply talking about the יום טוב of פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge. The ban on a large batch really applies to every יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing about the rule is unique to פסח. The תנא happened to be speaking in the context of פסח, so he stated the rule there, even though it applies more broadly.

keyTerms.meaning: He is standing in (discussing) this context

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the rule is specific to פסח. The ban comes from יום טוב rules, and פסח is just the setting the תנא was talking about.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so,
and this tanna
was discussing the Festival of Pesach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 10 by accepting it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the challenge (אין הכי נמי) and explaining the context of the wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule seemed to be limited to פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule applies to every יום טוב; פסח was just the context of the discussion.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms the dispute is about every Festival
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states the dispute in general terms: בית שמאי forbid baking פת עבה on יום טוב, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: בית שמאי say one may not bake פת עבה on יום טוב, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the previous answer. That ברייתא states the rule about יום טוב in general, not about פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the ruling is phrased as 'on a Festival,' with no mention of פסח. This confirms that the concern is about holiday work in general. It also shows that the ban is the view of בית שמאי, while בית הלל allow it.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban on baking a large batch is about יום טוב in general. It is the view of בית שמאי, and בית הלל permit it.

phrases.english: It was also taught so in a baraita:
Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹפִין פַּת עָבָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One may not bake pat ava on a Festival,
and Beit Hillel permit it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 11 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That the ban on פת עבה applies to every יום טוב
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the dispute of בית שמאי and בית הלל about יום טוב in general

steps.title: Which kinds of מצה fulfill the obligation
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one fulfills the מצוה of מצה with fine bread, coarse bread, or even מצה shaped into designs, although shaped מצה should not be made in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A person fulfills the מצוה with fine bread, with coarse bread, and with מצה shaped into designs on פסח. This is true even though they said one should not make shaped מצה on פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא about which kinds of מצה are valid for the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both high-quality and low-quality flour are valid. Decorated מצה is also valid after the fact (בדיעבד), even though one should not make it in the first place (לכתחילה). The next steps explain the reason for that first-place restriction.

keyTerms.meaning: Bread made of fine, sifted flour
מצה shaped or decorated with figures

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא says both that one fulfills the מצוה with shaped מצה and that one should not make it. There is no contradiction: it is valid after the fact, but should not be made in the first place.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One fulfills the obligation with fine bread,
and with coarse bread,
and with figure-shaped matzah on Pesach,
even though they said
one does not make figure-shaped matzah on Pesach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the types of מצה that are valid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fine, coarse, and shaped מצה all fulfill the מצוה, but shaped מצה should not be made in the first place.

steps.title: ביתוס בן זונין asks why shaped מצה is not made
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports that ביתוס בן זונין asked the חכמים why one may not make shaped מצה on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: ביתוס בן זונין asked the חכמים about this: Why did you say that one may not make shaped מצה on פסח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story in which someone asks the חכמים for the reason behind the restriction from Step 13. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave the rule without a reason. ביתוס's question opens a discussion about what is actually wrong with shaped מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who questioned the חכמים

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר זֶה שָׁאַל בַּיְיתּוֹס בֶּן זוֹנִין לַחֲכָמִים:
phrases.english: Baitos ben Zonin asked the Sages about this matter:
For what reason did they say
that one does not make figure-shaped matzah on Pesach?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the restriction stated in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason shaped מצה should not be made on פסח

steps.title: Shaping takes too long and the dough becomes חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that the woman spends too long shaping the dough, and it becomes חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Because the woman lingers over it and makes it become חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give their reason: decorating the dough takes time, and dough that sits too long rises.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is not about decoration itself. The problem is the delay, because the longer dough sits unbaked, the greater the risk that it becomes חמץ.

phrases.english: They said to him:
Because the woman lingers over it
and causes it to become leavened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ביתוס's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Shaping causes delay, and the delay leads to the dough becoming חמץ.

steps.title: Baitos suggests a mold that shapes the matzah instantly
steps.stepSummary: ביתוס argues that a mold could shape the מצה instantly, so there would be no delay.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: It is possible to make it with a mold and set the shape immediately!
steps.whatsHappening: ביתוס challenges the חכמים' reason. If the only problem is delay, a mold removes that problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים' reason was the time spent shaping. A mold presses the design in at once, so the risk of חמץ disappears and the ban should not apply.

phrases.english: He said to them:
It is possible to make it with a mold
and set its shape immediately!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that shaping causes delay
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A mold removes the delay, so the reason for the ban no longer applies.

steps.title: People would not understand the distinction
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reply that people would not grasp the difference. They would say all shaped מצה is forbidden except ביתוס's, so the ban stays for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: People will say, 'All shaped מצה is forbidden, but ביתוס's shaped מצה is permitted!'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים admit that a mold avoids the delay. Even so, they keep the ban for everyone, because an exception would confuse people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not with the mold itself. The problem is how it looks. Permitting molded מצה would seem like a special privilege for ביתוס, and people would not understand the reason. So the general ban stays in place without exceptions.
steps.whatToRemember: Shaped מצה is valid after the fact, but one should not make it. The worry is delay leading to חמץ. Even with a mold, the חכמים kept the ban for everyone, so that people would not be confused by an exception.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in rabbinic rules: a decree stays in force even where its reason does not apply, so that the public will not be confused by exceptions.

phrases.english: They said to him:
People will say: all shaped matzot are forbidden,
yet Baitos' shaped matzot are permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ביתוס's mold suggestion in Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Policy reasoning: the ban is kept so that the public is not misled
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With a mold there is no delay, so the מצה should be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban stays for everyone, because an exception would be misunderstood.

steps.title: Shaped מצה is served at רבן גמליאל's home
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בר צדוק tells how he and his father saw shaped מצה served at רבן גמליאל's home on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בר צדוק said: Once I followed my father into the home of רבן גמליאל, and they brought shaped מצה before him on פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that seems to clash with the ban from the last steps. It is setting up a question that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that the חכמים banned shaped מצה for everyone. Now we see a great leader, רבן גמליאל, eating shaped מצה on פסח. This makes us ask how that could be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: מצה shaped or decorated with designs
The נשיא, the leader of the generation

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok said:
Once I went in after my father
into the house of Rabban Gamliel,
and they brought before him
shaped matza on Passover.
phrases.notes: מצה made with designs or figures

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק: פַּעַם אַחַת נִכְנַסְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that seems to go against the ban explained in steps 15-17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shaped מצה was served at רבן גמליאל's table on פסח.

steps.title: The son asks how this is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks his father: didn't the חכמים forbid making shaped מצה on פסח?
steps.simpleTranslation: I said: Father, didn't the חכמים say that one may not make shaped מצה on פסח?
steps.whatsHappening: The son points out the conflict. The חכמים banned shaped מצה, yet it is being served here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge sets the known rule against what was done in רבן גמליאל's home. One of the two must be limited somehow.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't the חכמים say so? (a question that challenges)

phrases.english: I said: Father,
didn't the Sages say this:
one may not make shaped matza on Passover?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַרְתִּי: אַבָּא, לֹא כָּךְ אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the story in step 18 fits with the ban.
steps.kashyaTarget: The shaped מצה served at רבן גמליאל's home.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים forbade making shaped מצה, so how could it be served at רבן גמליאל's table?

steps.title: The ban is only for bakers
steps.stepSummary: רבי צדוק answers that the ban was said about professional bakers, not about ordinary people.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: My son, they did not say it about everyone. They said it only about bakers.
steps.whatsHappening: The father answers by limiting the ban to one group: professional bakers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bakers sell their מצה, so they want it to look perfect. They may spend too long shaping it, and the dough could become חמץ. A home baker is not under that pressure, so the ban does not apply to them.

phrases.english: He said to me: My son,
they did not say it about everyone's matza,
rather, they said it about bakers' matza.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שֶׁל כׇּל אָדָם אָמְרוּ, אֶלָּא שֶׁל נַחְתּוֹמִין אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on shaped מצה applies to everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban applies only to professional bakers, who might take too long to make it look perfect.

steps.title: Second version: the ban is for ordinary people
steps.stepSummary: Another version says the opposite. The ban is for ordinary people, not for bakers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say he told him this: They did not say it about bakers. They said it about everyone else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the father's answer, which flips the groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, bakers are experts and work fast, so they will not delay the dough. Ordinary people are slow at shaping, so they are the ones who might let it become חמץ. רבן גמליאל's מצה must have come from expert bakers.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (a second version of the same report)
This is what he said to him

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions agree that the ban covers only one group. They argue only about which group: bakers or ordinary people. Either way, shaped מצה that was already made may be eaten after the fact (בדיעבד).

phrases.english: Some say this is what he said to him:
they did not say it about bakers' matza,
rather, about everyone else's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the answer in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule (opposite group)
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban applies to ordinary people. Bakers are skilled and fast, so they are allowed.

steps.title: Thin shaped wafers are allowed, thick loaves are not
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי allows shaped מצה made thin like wafers, but not shaped מצה made thick like loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: One may make shaped מצה like thin wafers, but one may not make shaped מצה like thick loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives his own rule for when shaped מצה is allowed. It depends on how thick it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thick dough is more likely to become חמץ, so shaping it is risky. Thin wafers bake quickly and are less likely to rise, so shaping them is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban on shaped מצה is limited. It applies only to one group (bakers or ordinary people, depending on the version), and according to רבי יוסי only to thick loaves. Shaped מצה that was already made is still kosher for the מצוה after the fact.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
one may make shaped matza like thin wafers,
but one may not make shaped matza like thick loaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: עוֹשִׂין סְרִיקִין כְּמִין רְקִיקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another way to limit the ban, based on thickness instead of who is baking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thin shaped wafers are allowed. Thick shaped loaves are not, because they can become חמץ.

steps.title: A list of baked goods exempt from חלה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists several kinds of cakes and dough that are exempt from חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: sponge cakes, honey cakes, spiced cakes, חלת המסרת, and dough mixed with תרומה are exempt from חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא about which foods are exempt from separating חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of these items are not baked in a normal oven, so they may not count as 'bread' for חלה. The mixed dough (מדומע) is exempt for a different reason: it already contains תרומה. The next steps explain the unclear items.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
sponge cakes, honey cakes, and spiced cakes,
and pan bread, and dough mixed with teruma —
are exempt from challa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: חלה obligations for different kinds of baked goods.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These five items are exempt from חלה.

steps.title: What is חלת המסרת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the term חלת המסרת means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is חלת המסרת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of an unclear word in the ברייתא. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. It is a simple request to define a term so we know what food the ברייתא is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: Bread made in a deep pan

phrases.english: What is pan bread?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define a term from the ברייתא in step 23.

steps.title: It is scalded dough made by homeowners
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי explains that חלת המסרת is scalded dough made by regular homeowners.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: This is the חלוט of homeowners.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers the question and defines the term.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלוט is dough cooked with hot water, usually in a deep pan, not baked in an oven. That is why it may not count as normal bread for חלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Dough scalded or cooked with hot water

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
This is the scalded dough of homeowners.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: זֶה חָלוּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חלת המסרת is the scalded dough made by homeowners.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: exempt because they are pot-cooked
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says these items are exempt because they are cooked in a pot, not baked.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: These are pot-cooked foods.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains why the items in the ברייתא are exempt from חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלה applies to bread, which is baked. If dough is cooked in a pot (אילפס), it is not bread, so it is exempt.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
These are pot-cooked foods.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: הַלָּלוּ מַעֲשֵׂה אִילְפָּס הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for the exemption in the ברייתא of step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dough cooked in a pot is not bread, so it is exempt from חלה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: exempt because they are baked in the sun
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says pot-cooked dough is obligated in חלה. The ברייתא's items are exempt because they were baked in the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Pot-cooked dough is obligated in חלה. These items are exempt because they were made in the sun.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with ריש לקיש and gives a different reason for the exemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, dough cooked in a pot over a fire still counts as bread, so it needs חלה. The ברייתא's items are exempt only because they were baked by the sun and not by fire.
steps.confusionAlert: Both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש agree that the items in the ברייתא are exempt. They argue only about the reason, and about whether pot-cooked dough needs חלה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This argument decides if dough cooked in a pot over a fire needs חלה. ריש לקיש says no, and רבי יוחנן says yes.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Pot-cooked foods are obligated.
And these are exempt because they were made in the sun.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מַעֲשֵׂה אִילְפָּס חַיָּיבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with ריש לקיש in step 26 and gives a different reason for the exemption.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pot-cooked dough needs חלה. The ברייתא's items are exempt because they were baked in the sun, not over a fire.

steps.title: A ברייתא says pot-made cakes are obligated, against ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: cakes made in a pot are obligated in חלה, and cakes made in the sun are exempt. This seems to refute ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: sponge-cakes, honey cakes and spiced cakes, if made in a pot, are obligated in חלה. If made in the sun, they are exempt. This is a refutation of רבי שמעון בן לקיש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש with a ברייתא that clearly says dough made in a pot is obligated in חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said pot-cooking is not baking, so pot-made dough is exempt. This ברייתא says the exact opposite: pot-made cakes are obligated. It also fits רבי יוחנן perfectly, since he said the only exemption is for sun-baked dough.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (usually from a ברייתא)

phrases.english: They raised an objection: sponge-cakes, honey cakes, and spiced cakes,
if one made them in a pot, they are obligated (in חלה),
if made in the sun, they are exempt.
phrases.notes: This matches רבי יוחנן's explanation exactly.

phrases.english: This is a refutation of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's position from Step 26 using a ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן (Step 27).
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that pot-cooked dough is exempt from חלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly rules that cakes made in a pot are obligated, which contradicts ריש לקיש directly.

steps.title: עולא: The pot was heated first, then the dough was stuck on
steps.stepSummary: עולא defends ריש לקיש. The ברייתא is talking about a case where the pot was heated first and then the dough was pasted onto its hot walls, which counts as baking.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: רבי שמעון בן לקיש could tell you: what case are we dealing with here? Where one heated the pot first, and afterward stuck the dough onto it.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the challenge by limiting the ברייתא to a special case that ריש לקיש would agree is obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the empty pot is heated first and the dough is then stuck to its hot sides, the pot acts like an oven. That is real baking, so even ריש לקיש agrees it is obligated. ריש לקיש's exemption is only for dough that is truly cooked in the pot.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (a defense on someone's behalf)
What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrowed reading)
He stuck or pasted (the dough onto the pot's walls)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key distinction for the rest of this passage: heating first and then sticking the dough counts as baking, while sticking first and then heating does not.

phrases.english: Ulla said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְךָ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish could say to you:
With what are we dealing here?
Where he heated (the pot) and afterward stuck (the dough on it).
phrases.notes: The hot, dry pot works like an oven, so this is baking.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: אָמַר לְךָ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 28 by narrowing the case in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that any pot-made dough is obligated, against ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only means a heated pot with dough stuck on afterward. That is baking, and ריש לקיש agrees it is obligated.

steps.title: Why didn't the ברייתא teach the opposite pot case?
steps.stepSummary: If sticking the dough on first and heating afterward is exempt, the ברייתא should have taught that distinction within the pot case. Instead it switched to the sun case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he stuck the dough on first and heated it afterward, what is the law? You would say it is exempt. If so, instead of teaching in the last clause, 'made in the sun, exempt,' the ברייתא should have drawn the distinction within the pot case itself: 'When is this said? When he heated first and then stuck the dough on. But if he stuck it on first and then heated, it is exempt.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא's answer by pointing to how the ברייתא is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to עולא, the ברייתא has an exempt pot case close at hand: sticking the dough on first and heating afterward. A teacher would normally contrast two pot cases. Moving to an entirely different case, the sun, suggests the ברייתא does not know of any exempt pot case. That undermines עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: So too (that is indeed the law)
The last clause of a teaching
Let it distinguish and teach within the same case
In what case is this said? (a limiting formula)

phrases.english: But if he stuck it on and afterward heated it, what is the law?
So too, it would be exempt?
If so, instead of teaching in the last clause, 'made in the sun, exempt,'
let it distinguish and teach within that case itself:
In what case is this said?
For example, where he heated and afterward stuck the dough on,
but if he stuck it on and afterward heated, they are exempt?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks עולא's answer from Step 29 based on how the ברייתא is phrased.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's limiting reading of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an exempt pot case existed, the ברייתא would have contrasted it with the obligated pot case instead of switching to the sun.

steps.title: The ברייתא is missing words: the pot case is like the sun
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ברייתא is incomplete. It does teach the exempt pot case: sticking the dough on first and heating afterward counts like the sun and is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא is missing words, and this is what it teaches: When is this said? When he heated first and then stuck the dough on. But if he stuck it on first and then heated, it is as if he made it in the sun, and it is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the wording challenge by filling in words it says are missing from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the missing words added, the ברייתא does draw the distinction within the pot case. The sun clause stays, but now it is the comparison: dough stuck on first and heated afterward is treated like sun-baked dough, so it is exempt. ריש לקיש's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what it teaches

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the sun clause has been erased. It is still in the ברייתא; it now serves as the comparison for the pot case of sticking first and heating afterward.
steps.whatToRemember: According to ריש לקיש: heating the pot first and then sticking on the dough counts as baking, so it is obligated in חלה. Sticking on the dough first and then heating counts like sun-baking, so it is exempt.

phrases.english: It is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
In what case is this said?
Where he heated and afterward stuck the dough on,
but if he stuck it on and afterward heated,
it is as if he made them in the sun, and they are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of Step 30 by adding missing words to the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to skip the exempt pot case and jump to the sun instead.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא does include the exempt pot case, and it compares it to the sun case.

steps.title: Pot-made מצה works for the מצוה, so it counts as bread
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says one fulfills the מצוה of eating מצה with half-baked מצה and with מצה made in a pot. This suggests pot-made dough is bread, against ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One fulfills the obligation with half-baked מצה and with מצה made in a pot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to ריש לקיש from the laws of מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only bread can be used for the מצוה of מצה. If pot-made מצה works, then pot-made dough must count as bread. Bread is obligated in חלה, so this contradicts ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a source used as proof or challenge)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One fulfills the obligation with half-baked matza
and with matza made in a pot.
phrases.notes: This implies pot-made dough counts as bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to ריש לקיש, coming after the first challenge was resolved.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that pot-cooked dough is not bread
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pot-made מצה works for the מצוה, so pot-made dough is bread. Bread is obligated in חלה.

steps.title: Same answer: the pot was heated before the dough went on
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the same way: the ברייתא means the pot was heated first and the dough was stuck on afterward, which is real baking.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it means where he heated the pot first and afterward stuck the dough on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reuses עולא's distinction to answer the מצה challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pot-made מצה works only when the pot is heated first and acts like an oven. Then it is baked bread, which ריש לקיש agrees about. The ברייתא says nothing about dough that is truly cooked in the pot.
steps.whatToRemember: Both challenges to ריש לקיש are answered with one idea: a pot heated first, with the dough stuck on afterward, counts as baking.

phrases.english: Here too, it means where he heated and afterward stuck the dough on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 32 by applying עולא's answer from Step 29.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Pot-made מצה seemed to prove that any pot-made dough is bread.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only refers to a heated pot with dough stuck on afterward, which is baking.

steps.title: What counts as half-baked מצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the definition of מצה הינא, mentioned in the ברייתא earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'half-baked מצה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא in step 32 said you can use מצה הינא for the מצוה. Now the גמרא stops to ask what exactly that term means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Half-baked' is vague. How baked does it need to be to count as bread? The גמרא is asking for a clear line.

phrases.english: What is half-baked matza?
phrases.notes: Refers back to the ברייתא quoted in step 32.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ריש לקיש pot discussion and clarifies a different term from the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact baking level that makes מצה count as 'half-baked' but still valid.

steps.title: שמואל: no dough strands when you break it
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: מצה הינא is any מצה that, when broken, does not pull out strands of dough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Any מצה that, when you break it, has no threads of dough stretching out of it.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a simple physical test. Break the מצה. If no doughy strings stretch out, it is baked enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Raw dough is stretchy and pulls into strings. Once it stops doing that, it has become bread, even if it is not fully baked. That is the minimum level of baking.

keyTerms.meaning: Are pulled out or stretch out

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical test for whether partly baked מצה counts as bread for the מצוה.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Any matza that, when one breaks it,
no strands of dough stretch out from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מצה הינא is מצה baked enough that breaking it produces no dough strands.

steps.title: רבא: the same test applies to the תודה breads
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the same standard applies to the breads of the קרבן תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And the same is true for the breads of the תודה offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes שמואל's test and applies it to another case, the breads brought with a קרבן תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תודה offering comes with loaves of bread. רבא says that loaves baked only to שמואל's 'no strands' level are also valid there.

keyTerms.meaning: The loaves brought with the thanksgiving offering

phrases.english: Rava said: And likewise the loaves of the thanks-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends שמואל's definition to a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לחמי תודה baked only until no strands pull out are valid.

steps.title: Why did רבא need to say this? Both are called 'לחם'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: his point is obvious, because the תורה calls both מצה and the תודה loaves 'לחם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! Here it is written 'bread,' and there it is written 'bread'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבא bothered to teach this. Since both cases use the word 'לחם', the same definition should obviously apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is that רבא's statement adds nothing. If the תורה uses the same word in both places, the same standard of 'bread' should carry over automatically.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why say it?

phrases.english: It is obvious! Here, "bread" is written,
phrases.notes: For מצה, the תורה calls it 'לחם עוני'.

phrases.english: and there, "bread" is written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רבא's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement that לחמי תודה follow the same standard.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word 'לחם' appears in both places, so the shared definition is obvious and needs no teaching.

steps.title: We might have thought the תודה is different because of 'והקריב ממנו'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain why רבא's teaching was needed. A פסוק about the תודה, 'and he shall present from it', might have made us think the תודה has a different standard. The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since it is written 'And he shall present from it'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting its answer with 'מהו דתימא', meaning 'you might have thought.' It quotes a פסוק about the תודה to show why we might have treated it differently. The full answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer shows that the two cases are not as similar as the קשיא assumed. Something special in the תודה's פסוק could have pointed to a stricter standard. רבא teaches that, even so, the same test applies.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said; introduces a mistaken assumption that a teaching comes to block
And he shall present from it (ויקרא ז:יד)

steps.confusionAlert: This step is cut off in the middle. The quote of the פסוק and the explanation of why the תודה might be different continue on the next amud.

phrases.english: Lest you say,
since it is written: "And he shall present from it
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge by pointing to a special פסוק about the תודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows a reason we might have thought otherwise, so the teaching is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of the special wording 'והקריב ממנו', the תודה loaves might need a different (stricter) standard than ordinary 'לחם'.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא teaches that the תודה loaves still follow שמואל's 'no strands' test (explained further on the next amud).
